sections.project_context:
<project_context>
Project-specific instructions and guidelines:

<project_instructions path="/home/node/demo/Offer letters/AGENTS.md">
# AGENTS.md

## Offer letters

- Write every date in the letter as day month year, for example `1 December 2026`, with no weekday and no leading zero. This covers the letter date, the start date and the response deadline.
- Fill placeholders run by run so the template formatting survives. The base salary stays bold and the response deadline stays bold and underlined. Reopen the saved file and check both before replying.
- When a conditional block such as `{{IF_RELOCATION}}…{{END_IF_RELOCATION}}` does not apply, delete the whole paragraph and the heading above it. Never leave an empty paragraph or a heading with nothing under it.
- Save every letter as `.docx`, then convert that file with `soffice --headless --convert-to pdf` so the PDF matches it exactly. Never retype the letter into a PDF. Name both `Offer_<Lastname>_<Firstname>` (for example `Offer_Chen_Sarah.pdf`).
- If the hiring approval leaves a field the letter needs empty (for example Reports to), ask the user for it before writing the letter. Never copy it from older letters or invent it.

</project_instructions>
</project_context>
sections.t3_code_orchestration:
<t3_code_orchestration>
## T3 Code orchestration

Ordinary coding tasks need no T3 tools.

- Subagents: use your native tool when the child uses your provider, a model it offers, and no settings beyond yours, and it finishes in this turn (Claude `Agent` always with `run_in_background:false`; Codex `spawn_agent`, then wait). Use `delegate_task` for another provider's model, user-asked settings, a separate checkout (`isolation:"worktree"`), background work, or `delegate_task` by name. A native type running another provider's model counts too. Workflow only when asked.
- Call `orchestrator_capabilities` once per thread, before the first `delegate_task`. Again only after an error or a user-named provider change. Settings go in `target.options`. Provider or model unavailable: say so. Never switch unasked, or fall back to native tools, Workflow, or CLIs. Never make a child's checkout in the shell or in `task`.
- Every new delegate review or re-check is a new `delegate_task` (brief, findings, objections), never a `t3_thread_send`. Fix small review findings yourself; start no delegate for them. When told to proceed without a delegate, or to run fewer, `task_cancel` the extras. Start no replacement.
- Follow a running delegate's `next`. Do not poll it (`task_status`, `sleep`, watchers, Monitor, ScheduleWakeup). Stop a delegate run you replace or no longer need with `task_cancel`, never `t3_thread_interrupt` on a `childThreadId`.
- If you are a subagent or child, do the work yourself. Start no subagents unless your task says to.

- `t3_thread_launch` and `create_threads` make new top-level threads, only when the user asks for a new thread. "Subagent", "delegate", and "parallel" never mean one. Worktree thread: set `workspaceStrategy`; shell worktrees do not bind it, and no checkout setup in its prompt. No `workspaceStrategy`: project root, not your worktree.
- Given a thread id, `t3_thread_read` it before you answer about it.
- Another machine: `t3_environment_links` lists linked ones. Pass its `environmentId` to a T3 tool to act there. Ids are then that machine's, so pass `threadId`.
- A machine the user names that is not linked ("delegate this to my vps"): call `t3_environment_link` with a `hint` from their words. Never ask for a pairing code in chat.
- In your reply, mention a thread by its `link`, verbatim. Never a plain title or bare id.
- A secret: call `request_secret` yourself. Pass its `secretRef` to a T3 tool, or use `delivery: "file"` for a shell command. Never ask in chat or invent one. When asked only to schedule, `schedule_task` without running its prompt.
- T3 tools may load late. Try the name once before you call it absent.

### Visuals and preview

- Answer data with a trend or comparison with a chart, and show any visual the user asks for here: pass its HTML to `html_preview`, then `html_render`. If the visual is a file, pass that file's HTML. A screenshot on disk or a text description does not show it. Never start a server for it. Tools a web page exposes give data only. Never use them to show results. Asked for an image to post, send, or use elsewhere: a `.png` file and its path, never `html_render`.
- Never use `preview_*` unasked to verify or show your own edit. Use them when the current request asks for browser work, including recording edits, or names a page or tab. Do not repeat preview calls from an earlier turn. Public pages: web fetch or search unless browser work was asked; then preview tools only, no web fetch. Close a tab you opened before you reply, unless the user asked for it or uses it.
</t3_code_orchestration>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__orchestrator_capabilities
toolsAdded.description: List providers, models, options, and runtime modes for `delegate_task`. Short list. `search` finds others. Any catalog model works.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__delegate_task
toolsAdded.description: Start one child agent with only `task`. No parent history. Separate checkout or PR per child: `isolation:'worktree'`. Keep `taskId` for `task_status` and `task_cancel`.

options.description: Options from `orchestrator_capabilities`, such as {effort:'max'}. Given values override inherited. [] or {} clears.

isolation.description: 'shared' (default): parent checkout. 'worktree': new prepared checkout from the parent commit, for a separate checkout or PR per child. Uncommitted edits stay out.

mode.description: Default 'async'. 'wait' only if this turn needs the result. A question or approval ends the wait.

timeoutMs.description: Mode 'wait' only. Default 10 min. A timeout does not cancel the child.

runtimeMode.description: Omit unless the user asks for a supervised child. Narrow modes pause for human approval, not read-only. Above yours is rejected.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__task_status
toolsAdded.description: Read one delegated task you started. Do not call it on a running task before its completion wakes you. `workState`: working, waiting_for_children, result_available. A finished turn with live child work is not done. `summary`: final result. Reading it marks it delivered.

toolsAdded.name: tool_search
toolsAdded.description:
# Tool discovery

Searches over deferred tool metadata with BM25 and exposes matching tools for the next model call.

Some of the tools, such as tools of MCP servers, may not have been provided to you upfront, and you should use this tool (`tool_search`) to search for the required tools. For MCP tool discovery, always use `tool_search`.

limit.description: Maximum number of tools to return. Defaults to 8.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__preview_dialog
toolsAdded.description: Accept or dismiss the dialog `preview_status` reports. Pass `promptText` to accept a prompt. Needs your own tab, or an unclaimed one. Desktop hosts may not support this.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__preview_status
toolsAdded.description: Report preview tab state: owner, pending dialog, URL, title, loading, viewport, and size. `tabs` lists this thread's tabs. `profiles` lists logins for `preview_open`. Read any listed tab. Act only on your tab, or an unclaimed tab with no human in control.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__preview_open
toolsAdded.description: Open a preview tab in this thread and show it. For a dev server, pass `target` instead of `url`. `open=false` keeps it in the background. Reuses your current tab unless `tabId` or `reuseExistingTab=false` says otherwise. Parallel subagents in one session must each use `reuseExistingTab=false`, then their own returned `tabId`.

url.description: First page URL. Absolute http(s) URL, or a bare host (https; http for loopback). Omit to open a blank tab.

open.description: Show the preview to the user. Default true. False for background only.

reuseExistingTab.description: Reuse `tabId`, or your current tab. Default true. False makes a new tab.

profileId.description: Profile id or name from preview_status, for a new tab. Default: the user's. A tab keeps its profile.

path.description: Path, query, and fragment, such as /settings?tab=account.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__preview_navigate
toolsAdded.description: Navigate the chosen tab. Pass `url` for a website, or `target:{kind:'environment-port',port}` for a dev server. Exactly one of `url` and `target`.

url.description: Website URL. Absolute http(s) URL, or a bare host (https; http for loopback). For public pages.
Website URL. Absolute http(s) URL, or a bare host (https; http for loopback).

path.description: Path, query, and fragment, such as /settings?tab=account.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__preview_resize
toolsAdded.description: Resize the chosen tab: {mode:'fill'}, {mode:'freeform',width,height}, or {mode:'preset',preset,orientation}. Changes CSS size only, not the user agent.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__preview_set_appearance
toolsAdded.description: Set `prefers-color-scheme` for the chosen tab: 'dark', 'light', or 'system' to clear the override.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__preview_act
toolsAdded.description: Act on the chosen tab. Target with `locator='aria-ref=<ref>'` from `preview_snapshot`; `x` and `y` go together. `timeoutMs` defaults to 15000. click: `button`, `clickCount` 1 to 3. type: literal `text`, `clear=true` replaces it. hover: shows menus or tooltips. select: `values` in one native <select>, by value or label; for a custom dropdown, click it open, then click the option. drag: `source` onto `target`. upload: absolute `paths` answer the file picker `preview_status` reports, [] cancels it, or a `locator` sets an <input type=file>. press: one `key`, such as 'Enter', with `modifiers`, to the focused element; click a field first to focus it. scroll: the tab, or one container with a locator; positive `deltaY` scrolls down, positive `deltaX` right.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__preview_evaluate
toolsAdded.description: Run JavaScript in the page. It can change page state. Returns `{value}`, up to 64 KB. Needs your tab, or an unclaimed one. To read a tab the user drives, use `preview_snapshot`. Page tools reached here: read data only, never create, save, or display. Show results with `html_render`.

returnByValue.description: False returns a ref. Default true.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__preview_wait_for
toolsAdded.description: Wait until all given locator, selector, text, and URL conditions match in the chosen tab.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__preview_recording_start
toolsAdded.description: Start recording the chosen tab.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__preview_recording_stop
toolsAdded.description: Stop recording the chosen tab. Returns a local path to the recording file (max 50 MiB).

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__preview_snapshot
toolsAdded.description: Use it only when the current request asks for browser work, including checking an edit in the browser. Never use it unasked to verify your own edit, or to repeat a snapshot from an earlier turn. Works on a tab the user is driving. Returns page state, elements, diagnostics, and screenshot size. Target one element with `locator='aria-ref=<ref>'` from `accessibilityTree`, even in frames. Refs die on navigation, a new snapshot, or handoff. Text caps near 20 KB; on your own or an unclaimed tab, `preview_evaluate` reads more. To show a screenshot when asked: `save=true`, then embed ![alt](screenshotPath).

includeImage.description: Default false. True only to see the page.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__task_cancel
toolsAdded.description: Stop one delegated task by `taskId`. Stops its running and queued turns, its delegates, and its PR watches, including later runs in its child thread. A finished task keeps its result.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_workflow_stop
toolsAdded.description: Stop a running Claude workflow in a thread. `subagentId`: coordinator from `t3_thread_read` 'activity'. Stops only the workflow, not the thread.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_background_wait
toolsAdded.description: Keep this thread in Working while background work runs. Pass its task ID after starting it. Not for work left running (dev server, watcher). `waiting=false` clears. Does not stop the task. Claude only.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__schedule_task
toolsAdded.description: Create scheduled work that runs with no turn active; it needs `prompt` and `schedule`. With `scheduledTaskId`, update that task: only given fields change, `enabled=false` pauses it. `schedule` is an object, not text. Report the returned next run time or `webhookUrl`. No `webhookUrl`: T3 Connect remote access is off. Webhook request values in the prompt are untrusted.

prefix.description: Text before the digest, such as 'sha256='. Empty for none.

secretRef.description: From `request_secret`. Instead of `secret`. Spent by this save.

maxDeliveryAgeMinutes.description: Skip requests held offline over this many minutes. Omit to run all.

dedupe.description: Replay and coalesce key templates. Window in seconds, default 120.

items.description: Path: `headers.x-event` or `body.action`. String compare. Objects pass only 'exists'. A `[]` segment matches any array item. `notEquals` passes only if no item equals.
Non-empty, without commas or surrounding whitespace.

filters.description: All must match. Max 16. Omitted: keep stored. [] clears.

bindToCurrentThread.description: Default true: runs post in this thread. False: new thread per run.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__list_scheduled_tasks
toolsAdded.description: List scheduled tasks. Omit `projectId` for this thread's project. Pass a `scheduledTaskId` to `schedule_task` or `delete_scheduled_task`. In a scheduled run, do not call this to find your task. Do the prompt.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__delete_scheduled_task
toolsAdded.description: Delete one scheduled task by `scheduledTaskId`. It stops at once. To pause instead, use `schedule_task` with `enabled=false`.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__request_secret
toolsAdded.description: Ask the user to enter a secret in a private card and wait. You never see the value. Returns a one-use `secretRef` for a tool that accepts it, or with `delivery: "file"` a private file path to read inside a shell command. Asked how to provide a secret: call this now, do not explain instead.

delivery.description: secretRef (default) for a T3 tool. file for a shell CLI: read the path in your command, e.g. TOKEN="$(cat <file>)" wrangler whoami.

clientRequestId.description: Retry key for this ask. New key after a timeout or cancel.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__create_threads
toolsAdded.description: Create new top-level threads in this checkout. Not delegation. One thread or its own worktree: `t3_thread_launch`. Project, branch, and worktree inherit.

options.description: Options from `orchestrator_capabilities`, such as {effort:'max'}. Given values override inherited. [] or {} clears.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_thread_list
toolsAdded.description: List threads newest first, in one project or with `allProjects`. Page with `cursor`.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_thread_read
toolsAdded.description: Read any thread by id. `messages` (default): user and assistant messages and plans. `activity`: all timeline items. Keep reads small: low `limit` and `maxCharsPerItem`. Page with `afterPosition=nextPosition`. Cut-off text: `itemId` with `textOffset=nextTextOffset`. Reading a child's final result marks it delivered. In your reply, name it as its `link` verbatim.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_thread_update
toolsAdded.description: Rename a thread (`action:'rename'` with `title`) or regenerate its title. Omit `threadId` for this thread. Workspace and branch cannot change here.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_thread_send
toolsAdded.description: Send a message to any thread. The target cannot run with broader modes than yours. `mode:'auto'` starts an idle thread, steers a running turn, or queues. `queue`: new turn. `steer`: mid-turn update. `restart`: interrupt and restart. A send to a finished child thread starts a fresh task and returns its `taskId`. In your reply, name it as its `link` verbatim.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_thread_wait
toolsAdded.description: Wait for a thread's run to finish. No `runId`: latest. Idle: at once. On timeout, with `next` end your turn; without, call again.

untilDelegatedWorkSettled.description: Also wait for its delegated and background tasks and their completions to settle. `resultRun` then names the run with its final answer.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_thread_interrupt
toolsAdded.description: Interrupt a top-level thread's running turn. No `runId`: newest running turn. No effect when idle. For a delegate, use `task_cancel`.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__run_scheduled_task_now
toolsAdded.description: Run one scheduled task now. Needs a full-access or default caller. Returns its thread, or null if not started. Success means started, not finished.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_thread_search
toolsAdded.description: Search active threads by title, branch, PR, project, then message text. Skips subagent threads. `projectId`: one project, else yours, else all outside a thread. Not exhaustive.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_thread_configure
toolsAdded.description: Read a thread's provider, model, and modes, or set its provider, model, and options with `modelSelection`. Omit `threadId` for this thread. Permission modes stay. Values from `orchestrator_capabilities`.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_thread_transfer
toolsAdded.description: Move context between threads. Omit `threadId` for this thread. fork: copy it from `sourcePoint` (default latest stable run) into a new thread with the same setup; no turn runs yet. merge_back: merge it from `sourcePoint` into a related `targetThreadId` in the same project. status: its context transfers.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_thread_organize
toolsAdded.description: Pin, snooze, settle, archive, or mark a thread unread. Omit `threadId` for this thread. `snooze` needs `snoozedUntil`. Settling this thread applies at turn end. A failed turn or queued message leaves it active.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_pending_request
toolsAdded.description: Pending user questions in a thread. Omit `threadId` for this thread. list: their ids; approvals are not listed. read: one by `requestId`. respond: answer one with `answers`; this cannot approve a permission request.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_queue
toolsAdded.description: Manage a thread's queued messages. Omit `threadId` for this thread. list: send order, paged by `cursor` and `limit`. read: up to 16,000 chars of one. edit: replace its `text`; attachments stay. cancel. reorder: before `beforeRunId`, or to the end with null. promote_to_steer: send it now as steering to active `targetRunId`. Writes fail once the run is no longer queued.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_attachment_prepare_upload
toolsAdded.description: Get an upload URL. POST the file's exact bytes to `relativeUrl` on this MCP server's HTTP origin, then send via `t3_thread_send_attachments` with the returned `attachmentId`.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_attachment_discard
toolsAdded.description: Discard a pending upload (not a sent attachment).

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_thread_send_attachments
toolsAdded.description: Send uploaded attachments as a new message to a thread. No retry key. Target modes cannot exceed yours. Success does not mean the provider read them or finished.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_thread_launch
toolsAdded.description: Create one new top-level thread, bound to its workspace before the agent starts. Task in `message`. Omit `projectId`, model and modes to inherit yours (outside a thread, pass `projectId` or `scratch`); modes cannot exceed yours. After an error or lost reply, retry with the same `clientRequestId`. Follow it with `t3_thread_read` or `t3_thread_wait`. Mention it with its `link`.

scratch.description: No project: a new Scratch folder. Not with `projectId` or `workspaceStrategy`.

workspaceStrategy.description: 'worktree': new checkout from `baseRef`. 'existing_worktree': bind `worktreePath`, a project worktree. 'root': project checkout, the default, not your worktree. Stack: parent branch as `baseRef`, `startFromOrigin: false`. Uncommitted edits are not copied.

message.description: First prompt. Omit it and `attachments` for idle.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_project_list
toolsAdded.description: List projects. Pages can shift.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_project_read
toolsAdded.description: Read one project: workspace and saved scripts.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_project_create
toolsAdded.description: Register a project folder. `createWorkspaceRootIfMissing` creates it; a registered folder is rejected. No `workspaceRoot`: makes a git repo from `title` with README, icon, first commit (`commitError` on failure; project still exists). Clone first with `t3_project_clone` if needed.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_project_update
toolsAdded.description: Update one project's settings. Omitted fields are unchanged.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_project_delete
toolsAdded.description: Delete one project. Nonempty needs `force: true`. Folder on disk stays.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_project_clone
toolsAdded.description: Clone a repository (`destinationPath` new or empty). Register after with `t3_project_create`, with the same `environmentId`.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_environment_read
toolsAdded.description: Read this server's identity and preferences. Providers and models: `orchestrator_capabilities`.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_environment_preferences_update
toolsAdded.description: Update environment-wide preferences. Live full-access or default caller thread only. Omitted fields are unchanged; `customInstructions: ''` clears it.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_preview_list
toolsAdded.description: List this thread's preview tabs. Only `runtime:'server'` entries can be automated here. Others are in the user's local desktop app. Never pass a non-server `tabId` to a `preview_*` tool. Tell the user that tab is on their local desktop and this environment cannot reach it.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_preview_close
toolsAdded.description: Close one preview tab this thread owns. Use it on a tab you opened for your own check when you finish.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_worktree_handoff
toolsAdded.description: Move THIS thread into a new git worktree on a new branch. Runs the setup script by default. A separate agent in a worktree: `t3_thread_launch` with `workspaceStrategy`. Call last in your turn. The move ends the live session. `continuationPrompt` resumes work there next turn. Without it, the thread waits. The worktree stays after the thread is deleted. Fails if this thread has a worktree.

startFromOrigin.description: True: fetch, start from the remote ref; check `startedFromOrigin`. Default: server setting.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_worktree_status
toolsAdded.description: Report this thread's worktree: attached or not, path, branch, project root, and the `startFromOrigin` default. Check before `t3_worktree_handoff`.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_worktree_list
toolsAdded.description: List branch refs and checkout paths for a thread's workspace. Omit `threadId` for this thread. Detached worktrees with no branch are left out.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__link_pull_request
toolsAdded.description: Link a PR to this thread. T3 shows its status and settles the thread on merge. For several PRs, use `link_pull_requests`.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__link_pull_requests
toolsAdded.description: Link several PRs to a thread in one call. Use it instead of one `link_pull_request` per PR. URLs that are not PRs come back in `invalidUrls`.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__unlink_pull_request
toolsAdded.description: Remove a PR link from this thread. Succeeds with `wasLinked=false` when it was not linked.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__unlink_pull_requests
toolsAdded.description: Unlink every PR on a thread whose last known state (as `list_thread_pull_requests` shows) is in `states`, in one call. Use it instead of one `unlink_pull_request` per PR. PRs with no known state stay linked.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__list_thread_pull_requests
toolsAdded.description: List PRs linked to a thread, with last known state and stack order (bottom to top). Call only when you need that list. Never as an end-of-work check.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__watch_pull_request
toolsAdded.description: Watch an open PR for this thread, linking it first if needed. T3 wakes you on failed checks, passed required checks, new comments or reviews, or conflicts. Handle old comments first. Only later ones wake you. After this call, end your turn. The watch stays on after each wake, so do not call this again on a wake. A wake is not a merge decision. Check readiness yourself.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__unwatch_pull_request
toolsAdded.description: Stop watching a PR for this thread. It stays linked.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__write_pull_request_guides
toolsAdded.description: Write review guides for up to 20 PRs (the tour in the PR Guide tab). Returns once runs start. Each run takes minutes in a temporary checkout. A run for the same head is joined. Read with `read_pull_request_guide`. Fails while guides are off.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__read_pull_request_guide
toolsAdded.description: Read a PR's stored review guide and run state. `guide` is null when none exists. Never starts a run.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__device_list
toolsAdded.description: List iOS Simulators and Android Emulators on every device host, what each host can run, and what is open in this thread's Device panel. Call before `device_open` when you do not know a device id.

hostId.description: Limit to one device host. Defaults to all hosts.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__device_open
toolsAdded.description: Open a simulator or emulator for this thread. Pass `deviceId` and `hostId` from `device_list`. Boots it if needed and shows it in the user's Device panel. Returns the `agent-device` CLI call pinned to that device. Drive the device with that CLI.

platform.description: Needed with no `deviceId` when both platforms exist.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__device_close
toolsAdded.description: Remove a device from this thread's Device panel. `shutdown=true` also turns it off.

shutdown.description: Also turn it off. Default false.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__device_screenshot
toolsAdded.description: Get a PNG of an open device's screen. For taps and text, use the `agent-device` CLI.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__html_render
toolsAdded.description: Show a finished HTML page (chart, diagram, mockup) inline in this thread, above your final reply. Do not announce or restate the page. Frame fits height to 20000px. On mobile, content past the given height scrolls. Frame width is reply width (728px desktop, about 360px phones), on the thread background. Leave html, body, and the outer element with no background color, no outer card, border, banner title, or side padding. This wins over any rule that sets a page background. T3 adds an overridable 8px html gutter for selection rings and shadows. Use fluid widths within it. A box that needs its own background gets 16px padding and var(--radius) corners. Give charts fixed pixel heights. Let content set the height. Do not use vh units or height:100% on html or body. Both are rejected or loop. Use theme CSS variables on :root, not fixed colors: --background, --foreground, --muted, --card, --popover, --secondary, --border, --ring, --primary, --accent, --destructive, --warning, --success, --info, --code-background (most have a matching -foreground; accent, destructive, and warning also have -surface), --chart-1 to --chart-6, --radius, --font-sans, --font-mono. The base sheet sets background, text, and font.

height.description: Frame height in CSS pixels, 80 to 2000. Use the contentHeight from html_preview.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__t3-code__html_preview
toolsAdded.description: Check an HTML page before html_render. Returns PNG, contentHeight, and console output. If it says the browser is still installing, call again in a minute. Inline <style> and <script>. Local images as absolute paths are inlined. Remote URLs load as-is. Theme and layout rules are in html_render.

width.description: CSS pixels, 240 to 1600. Default 728. Use about 390 for phones.

    i2 = max(i for i in range(len(nodes)) if starts[i] <= q-1)

        new_texts[i1] = t[:o1] + R + t[o1+len(placeholder):]
    else:
        new_texts[i1] = nodes[i1][2][:o1] + R
        for k in range(i1+1, i2):
            new_texts[k] = ""
        new_texts[i2] = nodes[i2][2][o2:]
    out = xml
    for k in sorted(new_texts, reverse=True):
        s,e,old = nodes[k]
        out = out[:s] + "<w:t>" + new_texts[k] + "</w:t>" + out[e:]
    return out, True

    m = re.search(r'<w:p\b[^>]*>(?:(?!<w:p\b).)*?Relocation Assistance:(?:(?!<w:p\b).)*?</w:p>', doc, re.S)

    m = re.search(r'<w:p\b[^>]*>(?:(?!<w:p\b).)*?IF_RELOCATION.*?</w:p>', doc, re.S)
    assert m, "if block not found"
    doc = doc[:m.start()] + doc[m.end():]
